Install, update and find your worlds

Each installer builds the game from source and adds a launcher. Player worlds, editable data and shared preferences live outside the versioned application payloads; updates preserve them.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Before you install

You need an internet connection, several GB of free disk space and a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux the game runs in an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window.

Tip. Keep the extracted source folder until setup finishes. You can delete it afterwards.

Install on Linux

  1. Open a terminal in the extracted source folder.
  2. Run bash install.sh as your normal user. Do not use sudo; setup only uses it for system packages.
  3. Read the plan and confirm it. First setup installs compiler/audio tools and Rust, builds the game and adds a launcher. Existing Linux installations reuse their tools without administrator prompts; repair missing prerequisites separately.
  4. Choose qiqi in the application menu.
Key or actionWhat it does
--yesAccept the plan without asking
--prefix PATHInstall the app into another folder
--skip-prerequisitesSkip the tool install; use this on other distributions after installing the tools yourself (see docs/INSTALLING.md)
--helpShow the options; changes nothing

Setup never starts the game and never touches existing worlds.

Install on Windows

Careful. The Windows installer has not been tested on a real Windows PC yet.
  1. Double-click install-windows.cmd.
  2. Confirm the plan. If Windows asks, approve the Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer.
  3. Wait while setup downloads any missing Build Tools, Rust and FFmpeg, then builds the game.
  4. Choose qiqi in the Start menu. The shortcut has no game icon.

If the compiler setup asks you to restart Windows, restart it and run the installer again. Managed PCs may need an administrator to allow PowerShell scripts. In PowerShell, run install-windows.ps1 with the same options as the Linux installer: -Yes or -Prefix PATH.

Install on macOS

Careful. The macOS build is not validated yet. Graphics and sound are untested, and the game may fail to start on some Macs.
  1. Double-click Install-macOS.command and press Return to accept the plan.
  2. If Apple offers the Command Line Tools installer, finish it.
  3. If Homebrew asks for your password, enter your Mac password.
  4. Open Voxelgame.app from the Applications folder in your home folder.

The app is unsigned and not notarized. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. You can also run bash install.sh in Terminal. Do not turn off Gatekeeper.

On some Macs the F4 mode key needs Fn+F4.

Update the game

Linux managed installs can report their version, update from official source and select the previous verified installation. macOS and Windows have update scripts that rebuild the official source, but no version report or rollback yet.

  1. Save your world and close the game when convenient. Updating does not restart a running session; reopen afterwards to use the new release.
  2. From a clean official Git checkout, run bash install.sh --version, then bash install.sh --update. After archive setup, use ~/.local/share/voxelgame/app/launch.sh --version and --update instead. For a custom installation, use its launch.sh or the source script with --prefix PATH.
  3. Read the installed and available commit, build progress and final result. Linux needs Python 3.9+, Git, a prepared Rust/compiler toolchain and at least 5 GiB free. The update command does not install prerequisites or ask for administrator access.
  • Worlds, settings, screenshots and editable projects remain in their separate data folders.
  • Updates build official source in isolation and verify the completed files before switching the launcher. Dirty source checkouts cause a refusal; nothing is stashed or reset.
  • If fetching, building or verification fails, keep using the old launcher. Fix the reported network, disk-space or permission problem and retry.
  • Run bash install.sh --rollback to verify and select the previous release. Old releases are retained; updates do not delete them automatically.
  • Logs are under ~/.local/state/voxelgame/update-*.log unless the log folder was overridden.
Careful. Keep backups. Rollback switches application files only. An older executable may refuse worlds saved in a newer format; rollback does not undo changes to worlds or settings. Linux headless session preservation was checked; Windows and macOS updates have not been run on a real machine yet.

On macOS, close the game, extract a fresh complete source folder and double-click Update-macOS.command (or run bash update.sh). On Windows, close the game and double-click update-windows.cmd in a complete source folder. Both rebuild official `main` with the Git, Python 3.9+, Rust and compiler tools you already have, and need at least 5 GiB free. They keep your worlds and settings and the previous application files, and never install missing tools or ask for administrator access. They have no --version or --rollback; verified rollback is Linux only.

Where the files are

Key or actionWhat it does
LinuxWorlds and editable data: ~/.local/share/voxelgame/data (under $XDG_DATA_HOME if that is set). Installer logs: ~/.local/state/voxelgame
macOSWorlds and editable data: ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame. Installer logs: ~/Library/Logs/Voxelgame
WindowsWorlds and editable data: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\data. Installer logs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\logs

On Linux, shared display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/voxelgame/settings, defaulting to ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. Mode, environment controls and progression remain in the world file. Other platforms have not received native profile-location acceptance.

Setup writes a log once it starts, including runs that fail later. On Linux and macOS it prints the log path at the start, and a failed run does not repeat it. Windows prints the path at the end, including after a failure. A stop before setup starts, such as a cancelled plan, leaves no log. Its file name is install-<date>-<id>.log. On Linux and macOS, set VOXELGAME_INSTALL_LOG_DIR to change the log folder.

How worlds are stored

  1. Open Worlds and choose Create world. Enter a name, or leave it blank for a default name.
  2. Leave Seed blank for a fresh world, or enter a non-negative whole number. Choose Creative or Survival and a terrain generation; the default is generation 12.
  3. Use Tab or the Up/Down arrows to move between fields; Left/Right (or Space) change Mode and Terrain generation. Choose Create world or press Enter to confirm, or Cancel / Esc to return without creating it.

To reopen a world, select its row and choose Play world, press Enter, or double-click the row. Typing filters names; the mouse wheel, arrows and Page Up / Page Down browse the list. Worlds shows the selected save’s seed, mode and generation when those details can be read. Worlds: create, play, rename, duplicate and back up Choose and view a world seed

Use Rename (Ctrl+R) to change its display name, or Duplicate (Ctrl+D) to make a separately named playable copy. Rename keeps the save’s path. Duplicate saves the active local world first; stop hosting before duplicating it.

To delete a world, select it and hold Delete world (or the Delete key) for 3 seconds; letting go early cancels. Deleting removes the save, its name, preview and star for good. Backups you made are kept, so choose Create backup first if you might want the world back. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted: load another world first.

  • Each world has a .vxw save in the worlds folder inside the data folder, plus separate name, preview and session-history files when present.
  • A named new world uses a lowercase folder such as worlds/my-island/world.vxw. If that folder exists, a number is added. An empty name or a name with no usable letters or numbers gets world-0001, world-0002 and so on.
  • Stars live separately in worlds/favourites.txt. The last selected local world is recorded in worlds/last-world.txt.

Continue resumes your last local world

After a restart, Continue resumes the last successfully selected local save. If that record is missing or its file is gone, the fallback path is worlds/debug/debug.vxw. On a fresh installation with no saved world, Continue is disabled: choose Worlds to create one. An unreadable save opens a recovery dialog and is kept intact. Continue resumes the last selected local world

World mode, generator, time/weather/season controls and progression belong to that world. Display, audio, controls and accessibility preferences are shared across worlds. Untouched terrain is regenerated from the saved seed and generation.

Choose Create backup (Ctrl+B) for the selected world. The active local world is saved first; stop hosting before backing it up. The result names a completed snapshot under the data folder’s backups folder. Read Create and reopen a world backup for copying a snapshot back into Worlds.

Careful. The installer does not move worlds from a source checkout started with ./run.sh. Copying that worlds folder into the data folder with the game closed is inferred from the save paths and has not been tested in this wiki.

Requirements

Linux with a Vulkan graphics driver and an X11 or XWayland session is the tested platform. The Windows (64-bit Intel or AMD, Windows 10 or 11) and macOS (Apple Silicon, or Intel with a Metal GPU) installers are included, but no real machine has checked graphics and sound on them yet. System requirements and supported platforms

The first build needs internet access and several GB of free disk space. Software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is only a fallback for diagnostics.

Uninstall

There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its launcher by hand. Uninstalling

  • Linux: delete the app folder, `~/.local/share/voxelgame/app` by default, and `~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop`.
  • macOS: delete `~/Applications/Voxelgame.app`.
  • Windows: delete the app folder and the qiqi shortcut in your Start menu Programs folder. An earlier install may have left a Voxelgame shortcut too. The FFmpeg copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools` stays unless you delete it too.
  • Compilers, Rust, Homebrew and audio tools that setup installed stay on the PC.
Careful. Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds for good, so copy any world you want to keep first.

Build from source

Developers can build the game without the installer. With Rust 1.75 or newer and the Linux packages installed, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`. Build and run from source (cargo or ./run.sh)

  • `run.sh` rebuilds only when sources, assets or Cargo files are newer than the program. It shows a small Preparing the game window while it builds.
  • Started this way, worlds live in the worlds folder inside the source folder.
  • Optional: `aplay` (alsa-utils) for sound and `ffmpeg` for music.

The Linux menu entry and the macOS app use the Voxelgame cube icon. The Windows Start menu shortcut and the game window have no icon. App and launcher icon
